For convex sets represented inside a translated unit square, bounds discrepancy by $X^{\varepsilon}(X^{-1}+P^{2/3}X^{-2/3})$, uniformly in the position and the set, for $X\ge2$.
Taking the supremum over the manuscript's class of convex sets gives discrepancy $\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{-2/3+\varepsilon}$.

For a fixed convex body of positive area and $0<\kappa<1/2$, obtains relative error $O_{K_0,\kappa}(X^{-\kappa})$ at dilations $t\ge X^{-1/2+\kappa}$ that fit inside a translated unit square, uniformly over translations and rotations.
If $b_E(s)\le Bs^{\alpha}$ for $0<s\le1$, $0<\alpha\le1$ and $B\ge1$, gives $D_X(E)\ll_{\varepsilon}B^{2/(2+\alpha)}X^{-2\alpha/(2+\alpha)+\varepsilon}$ for $X\ge2$.

The difference measure, including diagonal pairs, has discrepancy $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(PX^{-1}+X^{-2})$ for a convex set of perimeter $P$ in a translated unit square. For a product of arcs of area $V$, the bound is $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(X^{-2}+V^{2/3}X^{-5/3})$, independently of its aspect ratio.

The variance of the normalized count is $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(P^2X^{-2}+A^{4/3}P^{2/3}X^{-5/3})$ for a convex set with area $A$ and perimeter $P$. Products of arcs satisfy $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(VX^{-2}+V^{5/3}X^{-5/3})$, and discs satisfy $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(r^2X^{-2}+r^{10/3}X^{-5/3})$. If every translate contains at most one point, the variance equals $|E|/N_X-|E|^2$.

For every fixed $s>0$, the $s$-th distance moment lies between constant multiples of $X^{-\vartheta(s)}$ and $X^{-\vartheta(s)+\varepsilon}$, where $\vartheta(s)=\min\{s,1+s/2\}$. Thus the exponents change at $s=2$.
For all real $N,X\ge1$ and $\eta>0$, $\sum_{N\le|r|<2N}|A_X(r,1)|^2\ll_\eta(NX)^\eta(NX^2+N^{1/3}X^{7/3})$. Both signs are included, with no relation between $N$ and $X$.
For real $R,Y\ge1$, the sum over $1\le|r|\le R$ is $\ll_\eta(RY)^\eta(RY^2+R^{1/3}Y^{7/3})$.
For $M,N,X\ge1$, $\sum_{|m|\le M,\ |n|\le N,\ (m,n)\ne(0,0)}|A_X(m,n)|^2\ll_\varepsilon(MNX)^\varepsilon\{MNX^2+(MN)^{1/3}X^{7/3}\}$. The axes and all signs are included.
For $X\ge2$ and $H\ge1$, the shell $\ell^2$ norm is $\ll_\eta(HX)^\eta(X^{-1}H+X^{-5/6}H^{1/3})$. Its square is $\ll_\eta(HX)^\eta(X^{-2}H^2+X^{-5/3}H^{2/3})$, and $|a_X(k)|^2\le1$.

[Pending]ambda H^{-\alpha}/[2(1-1/\pi)]$ for every real $H\ge1$.

For measurable $E\subset\mathbb T^2$ and $0<\delta\le1/8$, constructs smooth real $f_-\le\mathbf1_E\le f_+$ at every point, with values in $[0,1]$. The integral error is at most $b_E(3\delta)$; Fourier coefficients and shell norms gain $(1+\delta H)^{-L}$ with boundary errors $b_E(3\delta)$ and $b_E(3\delta)^{1/2}$ respectively.

For convex $\Omega\subset u+[0,1)^2$, $E=\pi\Omega$, perimeter $P$ and area $A$, proves $b_E(s)\le4\pi(Ps+s^2)$, $\|\mathbf1_E(\cdot+h)-\mathbf1_E\|_2^2\le P|h|_2$, Fourier tail $\ll P/T$, and $|\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(k)|\le\min(A,P/(4|k|_2))$ for $k\ne0$. Degenerate convex sets are included.

For $0<\delta\le1/8$ and $H\ge1$, with $b=P\delta+\delta^2$, the brackets have integral error $\ll b$, shell norm $\ll_L(1+\delta H)^{-L}(P^{1/2}H^{-1/2}+b^{1/2})$, and coefficient bound $\ll_L(1+\delta H)^{-L}(P/H+b)$.

For any measurable $E$ with $b_E(s)\le C_0(Ps+s^2)$ for $0<s\le1$, subdivision of a translation gives $\|\mathbf1_E(\cdot+h)-\mathbf1_E\|_1\le C_0P|h|_2$ for $|h|_2<1$. The separate convex slicing argument supplies the sharper constant used in (2.20).

For $X\ge2$, smooth counting error is $\sum_{k
e0}\widehat f(k)a_X(k)$, smooth difference-distribution error is $\sum_{k
e0}\widehat f(k)|a_X(k)|^2$, and for every measurable $E$ the translation variance is $\sum_{k
e0}|\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(k)|^2|a_X(k)|^2$.

For $C_E(v)=\int\mathbf1_E(x)\mathbf1_E(x+v)\,dx$, direct expansion gives $\mathcal V_X(E)=\int C_E\,d\nu_X-|E|^2$. The variance theorem uses the Fourier variance identity directly, independently of the difference-distribution theorem.
Controls the dyadic sum of $H^s(1+\delta H)^{-L}$ by $\delta^{-s}$ for $s>0$ and by a constant for $s<0$, with $L>\max(s,0)$ and $0<\delta\le1$.
At any $0<\delta\le1/8$, controls convex discrepancy by the boundary error $b=P\delta+\delta^2$ and the Fourier contributions with scales $X^{-1}\delta^{-1/2}$ and $X^{-5/6}$.
For convex sets in a translated unit square, gives the absolute-constant bound $D_X(\pi\Omega)\ll X^{-2}+\min(w_1,w_2)\ll X^{-2}+P(\Omega)$ for $X\ge2$.
For real $X\ge4$ and $0\le p\le X^{-1}$, the largest discrepancy among convex sets of perimeter at most p has order $p+X^{-2}$, with absolute constants.

A thin rectangle containing many diagonal reciprocal points has discrepancy $\gg X^{-1}$ while its perimeter contribution is $O(X^{-4/3})$, so the baseline term in Theorem 1.1 remains necessary even for positive-area convex bodies.
For the Euclidean definition of gamma-well-shapedness inside $[0,1)^2$, gives discrepancy $\ll_{\varepsilon}(1+\gamma)^{2/3}X^{-2/3+\varepsilon}$, uniformly for $\gamma\ge0$ and $X\ge2$.
Applies the boundary theorem to a Koch snowflake inside the unit square, with $\alpha=2-\log 4/\log 3$, giving exponent $0.539\ldots$; the same domain is not gamma-well-shaped for any finite gamma.

The finite set $E=\mathcal P_X$ has indicator zero almost everywhere but discrepancy one. Thus almost-everywhere or distributional-perimeter information cannot replace the stated pointwise/topological boundary control.

An arc of length $a$ admits smooth upper and lower brackets with integral error at most $4\delta$. With $a'=\min(1,a+4\delta)$, their coefficients are $\ll_L\min\{a',(1+|m|)^{-1}\}(1+\delta|m|)^{-L}$.

For $0<\kappa<1$, a fixed positive-area convex shape at linear scale $t\ge X^{-1+\kappa}$ has relative difference-count error $O(X^{-\kappa/2})$, uniformly in position and orientation within a translated unit square. Products of arcs have the same error when their area is at least $X^{-2+\kappa}$. Both conclusions hold with and without diagonal pairs under the corresponding normalizations.

If every translate of a measurable set contains at most one point, its normalized-count variance is $|E|/N_X-|E|^2$. A sufficient condition is containment, after projection, in a strip of width below $X^{-2}$; the stated small-perimeter, narrow-rectangle and small-disc cases follow.

For a fixed positive-area convex shape at scale $t\ge X^{-1+\kappa}$, the centers with relative count error greater than $\lambda$ have measure $\ll_{K_0,\kappa}\lambda^{-2}X^{-3\kappa/2}$, uniformly over admissible rotations and scales, for $0<\kappa<1$ and $0<\lambda\le1$.

For $r_0\le r\le1/4$, a single exceptional set has measure $\ll_\varepsilon\lambda^{-3}X^\varepsilon(X^{-2}r_0^{-2}+X^{-5/3}r_0^{-2/3})$ and outside it every disc count has relative error $O(\lambda)$. Open and closed discs are included. Taking $r_0=X^{-1+\kappa}$ and $\lambda=X^{-\kappa/3}$ yields exceptional measure $\ll_\kappa X^{-\kappa/2}$ for sufficiently large $X$.
